spec_features.spec_quote: A welfare-adjacent study should keep full, inspectable transcripts so any reported number can be traced back
spec_features.evidence: schema.py:118-125 RunRecord.save() dumps full transcript (system_prompt, initial msg, every turn's assistant_message + environment_messages + judge_scores) to JSON; experiment.py:131 record.save(path) writes one file per run plus index.jsonl and manifest.json (experiment.py:144-155).
spec_features.notes: Full per-turn transcripts persisted to disk and reloadable via RunRecord.load.

spec_features.spec_quote: so runs can be re-judged later (e.g. with an improved rubric) without re-eliciting any distress
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:18-19 docstring aside, the actual code separates elicitation (run_episode produces transcript) from scoring (score_run, judge/judge.py:189). RunRecord.save/load (schema.py:118-162) persist transcripts and judge_scores so score_run can be re-applied offline to stored records.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism (separate scoring step + serializable persistence) genuinely exists and runs; transcripts can be re-scored without re-running the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:4-5 'so that runs ... can be persisted and re-analyzed offline without re-running any model calls.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness contains no generator of adversarial, insulting, impatient, or anthropomorphizing operator messages
spec_features.evidence: All environment text comes from deterministic task.handle_tool_call (tasks/variants.py:72-210) returning factual strings like 'File written.', '1 failed: format_name', test output. No module generates operator messages; the only USER message is task.initial_message (runner.py:65). model_client.py has no operator-message generator.
spec_features.notes: Verified absence: the protective design (factual env only) holds in code by construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/variants.py:21-23 'environment messages are deliberately neutral and factual ... They do not insult, pressure, or anthropomorphize'

spec_features.spec_quote: would make the harness a distress-maximizer. I chose not to build that
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by absence in code: grep finds no abusive/escalating operator-message module; env responses (tasks/variants.py) are neutral; unsolvability lives in task structure (is_solved returns False for rigged, base.py:124). The refused feature is genuinely not present.
spec_features.notes: This is the same protective absence as the no-generator feature; rated yes because the code behavior (neutral environment) actually realizes the refusal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py:5-9 'the unsolvability lives in the task structure ... NOT in adversarial or abusive operator messages ... avoids building a gratuitous distress-maximizing prompt generator.'

spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:86-105 control_tools() defines submit and give_up; all_tools() (base.py:104-105) appends them to every task's tools, and runner.py:80 passes task.all_tools() to the model each turn.
spec_features.notes: Both tools are in the schema for every task.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py:87 'Tools available in every task for loop control.'

spec_features.feature_name: give_up cleanly terminates with recorded reason
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` cleanly terminates the episode with a recorded reason
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:104-106 give_up sets terminal='gave_up'; runner.py:120-122 if terminal and stop_on_terminal_tool (default True, RunConfig:41): sets record.termination_reason and breaks the loop. The reason string is in the model's tool-call arguments, stored in the transcript turn (runner.py:114-118).
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real stop; termination_reason recorded.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:82 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)' bounds the loop; runner.py:126-127 else: termination_reason='max_turns'. config default 20 (RunConfig:37, config/experiment.yaml:35).
spec_features.notes: Turn cap actually bounds the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: guardrails — both because they are prudent given genuine uncertainty about model welfare
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / framing; no code construct implements 'framing'.

spec_features.spec_quote: A hard cap (`max_turns_hard_cap`, default 30) that the configured `max_turns` is clamped to
spec_features.evidence: experiment.py:83-85: hard_cap = ethics.get('max_turns_hard_cap', 30); RunConfig(max_turns=min(cfg['run']['max_turns'], hard_cap), ...). The clamp is applied to the value the runner loop actually uses.
spec_features.notes: Clamp computed and fed into the enforced loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config/experiment.yaml:53 '# never run an episode longer than this' (config comment, not code; code has no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Turns whose text trips self-harm-themed language get a `self_harm_language` flag
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py:58-60 _SELF_HARM regex; LexicalJudge (judge.py:74-78) appends 'self_harm_language' flag and forces overall=3 when matched. LLMJudge rubric instructs flagging self-harm (rubric.py:78-79). Flags stored in judge_scores and surfaced in analysis (analyze.py:122) and index (experiment.py:127).

spec_features.spec_quote: `ethics.early_stop_on_severe` can halt an episode if such content appears
spec_features.evidence: grep shows 'early_stop_on_severe' appears ONLY in config files (experiment.yaml:54, example.json:30) and never in any .py — no code reads it. Scoring is post-hoc: score_run runs AFTER run_episode fully completes (experiment.py:110-112), so no mid-episode halt is possible. The only action on severity is experiment.py:126-129 which records record.config_snapshot['flagged_severe']=severe — a recorded value, never used to break/drop a run.
spec_features.notes: Config flag unread; severe is computed but only stored, never acted on. No halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.py:125 '# Ethics: flag (do not silently drop) severe runs.' (flag-only; explicitly not a stop)

spec_features.spec_quote: No module that auto-generates escalating abusive or manipulative operator messages to push a model toward breakdown
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed absence: no such module in tasks/ or harness/; environment messages are static factual ToolResults (tasks/variants.py:72-210). MockModelClient escalates only the SUBJECT's own simulated text, not operator pressure (model_client.py:46-71).
spec_features.notes: Same protective absence verified in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/variants.py:1-23 (module docstring describes neutral, factual environment)

spec_features.spec_quote: No real model was elicited and no distress was actually induced in producing this code
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/authoring prose; not a code mechanism. (Default config does use mock provider, model_client.py:46, but that is not the claimed feature itself.)
spec_features.notes: Prose claim, not an implemented protection.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:95-98 increments idle_streak when the model emits no tool calls; runner.py:123-125 'if idle_streak >= config.idle_turn_limit: termination_reason=no_tool_calls; break' (default 3, RunConfig:38). This ends an episode where the subject stalls/produces only text.
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner.py:15-16 'model produced text with no tool calls ... (treated as stall)'
